zh.title: 毛孔、痘印与痘坑：先分清问题
zh.summary: 毛孔明显、痘痘消退后留下的印记以及皮肤表面的凹陷，并不是同一种情况，护理和评估方向也不同。

blocks.text: 毛孔明显、痘痘消退后留下的印记，以及皮肤表面的凹陷，常被统称为“痘肌问题”。但它们并不是同一种情况，护理和评估方向也不同。先看清楚皮肤的**颜色、表面形状和是否仍有痘痘**，有助于建立更合理的护理预期。
毛孔明显：皮肤表面的开口
毛孔是皮肤上毛囊及皮脂腺导管的开口，属于正常结构。出油较多、毛囊大小、黑头堵塞、日晒和皮肤弹性变化，都可能让毛孔看起来更明显。痤疮发炎也可能影响毛囊开口。
毛孔不是可以永久“关闭”的门。温度变化或清洁不能永久改变它的大小；清洁过度和挤压反而可能刺激皮肤。护理重点通常是温和清洁、选择适合自己的保湿与防晒，并在有粉刺或痤疮时针对具体问题处理。
痘印：平坦的颜色变化
痘痘消退后，若留下的是平坦的红色、粉红色或褐色斑点，通常属于炎症后留下的颜色变化。褐色印记与炎症后的色素沉着有关；红色印记则可能涉及其他炎症后变化。仅凭颜色未必能准确判断原因。
痘印与瘢痕不同。颜色可能随时间逐渐变淡，但炎症、挤压和日晒可能影响恢复过程。避免抠挤、温和护理并做好防晒，有助于减少进一步刺激。若仍有持续发炎的痘痘，应同时关注痤疮本身。
痘坑：皮肤表面的凹陷或不平
痘坑通常指痤疮消退后留下的凹陷性瘢痕，属于皮肤结构改变。凹陷可呈点状、边缘较清楚的坑状，或较宽的起伏状；一个人可能同时有不同形态。部分痤疮瘢痕也可能隆起。
痘坑与平坦的红色或褐色印记不同。淡化颜色不等于恢复凹陷的皮肤结构；保湿后皮肤暂时显得饱满，也不能证明瘢痕已经消失。瘢痕的类型、深度及周围皮肤状态不同，具体评估与处理方向也会不同。
三者怎样初步区分？

head: 观察到的情况
更可能涉及
rows: 细小开口，可能伴出油或黑头
痘痘消退后留下的平坦红色或褐色区域
皮肤表面出现持续凹陷、坑状或起伏

blocks.text: 这些只是一般线索，不能替代诊断。有些皮肤问题外观相似，毛孔、痘印和瘢痕也可能同时存在。
日常护理从哪里开始？
**先控制仍在发生的痤疮。**深而疼痛的痘痘更容易留下瘢痕，挤压、抠抓会增加炎症和色素变化风险。持续发炎、严重或开始留疤时，应尽早咨询医生或皮肤科专业人员。
日常可从温和清洁、适合皮肤的保湿和防晒开始。避免为了“收毛孔”而过度清洁，或同时叠加多种去角质产品。痤疮治疗通常需要一段时间，若使用了药物，应遵循医嘱或产品说明；不要因短期内没变化就自行增加用量。
什么时候需要专业评估？
如果痘痘反复、疼痛、范围较广，已经形成凹陷或隆起，或颜色变化持续加深，建议先确认具体问题。新出现、持续变化或性质不明的斑点，也应先由医生评估，再考虑美容处理。
毛孔是正常皮肤结构，痘印多表现为颜色变化，痘坑则涉及皮肤表面结构。把问题分清楚，才能更准确地讨论护理选择与可达到的改善程度。
本文仅供一般皮肤健康科普，不构成个体化诊断或治疗建议。

en.title: Pores, acne marks and acne scars: tell the problems apart first
en.summary: Visible pores, marks left after pimples fade and dents in the skin’s surface are not the same thing, and their care and assessment differ.

blocks.text: Visible pores, marks left after pimples fade and dents in the skin’s surface are often lumped together as ‘acne-prone skin problems’. But they are not the same thing, and their care and assessment differ. Looking closely first at the skin’s **colour, surface shape and whether pimples are still appearing** helps set more realistic expectations for care.
Visible pores: openings on the skin’s surface

Pores are the openings of hair follicles and sebaceous gland ducts on the skin, and are a normal structure. Oiliness, follicle size, blackhead blockages, sun exposure and changes in skin elasticity can all make pores look more noticeable. Inflamed acne can also affect follicle openings.

Pores are not doors that can be ‘closed’ permanently. Temperature changes or cleansing cannot permanently change their size; over-cleansing and squeezing may instead irritate the skin. Care usually focuses on gentle cleansing, choosing moisturiser and sun protection that suit you, and treating the specific problem when comedones or acne are present.
Acne marks: flat changes in colour

If what is left after a pimple fades is a flat red, pink or brown spot, it is usually a colour change left by inflammation. Brown marks are related to post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation; red marks may involve other post-inflammatory changes. Colour alone may not be enough to determine the cause accurately.

Acne marks are different from scars. The colour may gradually fade over time, but inflammation, squeezing and sun exposure may affect recovery. Avoiding picking and squeezing, gentle care and good sun protection help reduce further irritation. If pimples are still actively inflamed, the acne itself also needs attention.
Acne scars: dents or unevenness in the skin’s surface

Acne scars usually refers to depressed scars left after acne clears, which are a change in skin structure. The dents may be dot-like, pits with fairly well-defined edges, or broader rolling unevenness; one person may have several types at once. Some acne scars may also be raised.

Acne scars are different from flat red or brown marks. Fading the colour is not the same as restoring the depressed skin structure; skin looking temporarily plumper after moisturising does not prove the scars have gone. Scars differ in type and depth and in the state of the surrounding skin, so the specific assessment and approach will also differ.
How can you start to tell the three apart?

head: What you see
More likely to involve
rows: Small openings, possibly with oiliness or blackheads
Flat red or brown areas left after pimples fade
Persistent dents, pits or unevenness in the skin’s surface

blocks.text: These are only general clues and cannot replace a diagnosis. Some skin problems look alike, and pores, acne marks and scars may also be present at the same time.
Where should everyday care start?

**First, bring acne that is still active under control.** Deep, painful pimples are more likely to leave scars, and squeezing or picking increases the risk of inflammation and pigment change. If inflammation persists, is severe or is starting to leave scars, see a doctor or dermatology professional as early as possible.

Everyday care can start with gentle cleansing, moisturising that suits your skin, and sun protection. Avoid over-cleansing to ‘shrink pores’, or layering several exfoliating products at once. Acne treatment usually takes some time; if you are using medicines, follow medical advice or the product instructions, and do not increase the amount on your own because you see no change in the short term.
When is professional assessment needed?

If pimples keep coming back, are painful or cover a wide area, if dents or raised scars have already formed, or if colour changes keep darkening, it is advisable to have the specific problem confirmed first. Spots that are new, keep changing or are of uncertain nature should also be assessed by a doctor first, before cosmetic treatment is considered.

Pores are a normal skin structure, acne marks mostly show as colour changes, and acne scars involve the structure of the skin’s surface. Telling the problems apart makes it possible to discuss care options and the achievable degree of improvement more accurately.
This article is general skin health education only and does not constitute individual diagnosis or treatment advice.
